paper_title: A Generative-AI-Driven Claim Retrieval System Capable of Detecting and   Retrieving Claims from Social Media Platforms in Multiple Languages
caption_used: Number of participants (N=6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial. The horizontal bar chart displays seven criteria ranked by participant endorsement. Relevant FCs was unanimously selected by all 6 participants, followed by FC Summary at 5. Relevance Explanation and Clarity and Simplicity each received 3 endorsements. Overall Summary was highlighted by 2 participants, while Filters and Veracity Explanation each received 1. Notably, the top three criteria — Relevant FCs, FC Summary, and Relevance Explanation — together account for approximately 82% of all endorsements, indicating a strong consensus around content retrieval and summarization features over interface and transparency elements such as Filters and Veracity Explanation.
model_annotation: The horizontal bar chart illustrates the number of participants (N=6) who identified each of seven evaluation criteria as beneficial in assessing a generative-AI-driven claim retrieval system, with bars ordered from highest to lowest endorsement. The vertical axis lists the criteria: “Relevant FCs,” “FC Summary,” “Relevance Explanation,” “Clarity and Simplicity,” “Overall Summary,” “Filters,” and “Veracity Explanation,” while the horizontal axis represents the “Number of Participants,” scaled from 0 to 6 in increments of 2. The bar for “Relevant FCs” (dark purple) extends to 6, indicating unanimous selection; “FC Summary” (dark blue) reaches 5; “Relevance Explanation” (teal) and “Clarity and Simplicity” (green-teal) both extend to 3; “Overall Summary” (light green) reaches 2; and both “Filters” (lighter green) and “Veracity Explanation” (lime green) extend to 1. The top three criteria—Relevant FCs, FC Summary, and Relevance Explanation—collectively account for 14 out of 17 total endorsements (approximately 82%), visually emphasizing participant prioritization of content-focused features over interface or transparency elements. The bars are sorted in descending order of endorsement, with no additional annotations or shading beyond the color-coded bars and numerical labels at their ends.
